Class SimpleRayTracer

java.lang.Object
renderer.RayTracerBase
renderer.SimpleRayTracer
class SimpleRayTracer extends RayTracerBase
A ray tracer implementing the Phong reflection model with Global Illumination. Supports partial-transparency shadows, soft shadows via area-light super-sampling, glossy reflections, diffuse (blurry) transparency, and full recursive GI.

Soft-shadow dependency: LightSource.getSize() must be implemented by every concrete light type (PointLight returns its radius field, SpotLight inherits, DirectionalLight returns 0).

Glossy / diffuse dependency: Material.kBlurR and Material.kBlurT control the beam spread for glossy reflection and diffuse transparency respectively. 0 = ideal (no blur).

    • TARGET_DISTANCE

      private static final double TARGET_DISTANCE
      Distance from the surface point along the ideal secondary ray at which the virtual target sampling area is placed for glossy / diffuse glass effects.

      With TARGET_DISTANCE = 100, the material blur parameter (kBlurR or kBlurT) is interpreted as a gradient percentage: blur = 5 spreads the beam ±5 units at 100 units depth, equivalent to a half-angle of arctan(5/100) ≈ 2.86°.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • calcGlobalEffects

      private Color calcGlobalEffects(Intersectable.Intersection gp, int level, Double3 k)
      Computes recursive reflection and refraction (global) color contributions.

      For each effect the material blur parameter selects the rendering mode:

      • kBlurR == 0 — perfect mirror: single ideal reflection ray.
      • kBlurR > 0 — glossy surface: beam of rays spread around the ideal reflection direction via calcGlobalEffectBeam(Intersectable.Intersection, Vector, double, int, Double3, Double3).
      • kBlurT == 0 — clear glass: single ideal refraction ray.
      • kBlurT > 0 — diffuse (blurry) glass: beam of rays spread around the incoming ray direction via calcGlobalEffectBeam(Intersectable.Intersection, Vector, double, int, Double3, Double3).
      Parameters:
      gp - the current intersection (must have n, v, vn set)
      level - remaining recursion depth
      k - accumulated attenuation factor
      Returns:
      the combined global color contribution

    • calcGlobalEffectBeam

      private Color calcGlobalEffectBeam(Intersectable.Intersection gp, Vector idealDir, double blur, int level, Double3 kx, Double3 k)
      Computes a glossy reflection or diffuse transparency contribution by tracing a beam of rays distributed around the ideal secondary ray direction.

      Algorithm

      1. A virtual target area is placed on the ideal secondary ray at distance TARGET_DISTANCE; its half-extent equals blur.
      2. A Blackboard generates DEFAULT_GLOSSY_SAMPLES sample points across that area, with a basis orthogonal to idealDir.
      3. For each sample, a secondary ray is cast from the surface point toward the sample. Rays that cross to the wrong side of the surface (n · sampleDir opposite sign to n · idealDir) are discarded — preventing light from leaking through at grazing angles.
      4. The colors of all valid rays (each already attenuated by kx inside calcGlobalEffect(Ray, int, Double3, Double3)) are averaged. If no valid sample exists, the single ideal ray is used as a fallback.

      Note: unlike soft shadows, wrong-side samples are excluded from both numerator and denominator, because for glossy surfaces the average represents the fraction of the visible cone — not the fraction of a light disk.

      Parameters:
      gp - the current intersection
      idealDir - the ideal secondary ray direction (normalized)
      blur - the material blur parameter (kBlurR or kBlurT); interpreted as the target area half-extent at TARGET_DISTANCE
      level - remaining recursion depth
      kx - material effect coefficient (kR or kT)
      k - accumulated attenuation factor
      Returns:
      the averaged attenuated color contribution of the beam

    • transparency

      private Double3 transparency(Intersectable.Intersection intersection)
      Computes the accumulated transparency factor (ktr) from the shaded point to the current light source.

      Dispatches to singleRayTransparency(Point, Vector, Vector, double) when lightSize == 0 (point/directional light, hard shadow) or softShadowTransparency(Intersectable.Intersection, Vector, double, double) when lightSize > 0 (area light, soft shadow with penumbra).

      Parameters:
      intersection - the current intersection (light cache must be populated)
      Returns:
      kT factor: Double3.ONE = unblocked, Double3.ZERO = full shadow

    • singleRayTransparency

      private Double3 singleRayTransparency(Point origin, Vector direction, Vector normal, double maxDistance)
      Casts a single shadow ray and returns the accumulated transparency factor of every geometry it passes through up to maxDistance.
      Parameters:
      origin - surface point from which the shadow ray is fired
      direction - direction toward the light source (or sample point)
      normal - surface normal, used to offset the ray origin by ±DELTA
      maxDistance - maximum distance to check for blocking geometry
      Returns:
      Double3.ONE if unblocked, Double3.ZERO if fully blocked, or a component-wise product of blocking materials' kT values

    • softShadowTransparency

      private Double3 softShadowTransparency(Intersectable.Intersection intersection, Vector pointToLight, double maxDistance, double lightSize)
      Computes soft shadows by sampling DEFAULT_SHADOW_SAMPLES points on the light source area and averaging the per-sample transparency factors.

      The target area is centered at the light position with its basis orthogonal to intersection.l. Wrong-side samples (the "sunset effect") contribute 0 ktr but are counted in the denominator, as required by the spec.

      Parameters:
      intersection - the current intersection (light cache must be populated)
      pointToLight - direction from surface toward the light center
      maxDistance - distance from surface to the light center
      lightSize - radius of the light source area (must be > 0)
      Returns:
      the averaged ktr across all samples
